_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Vietnam covering Ông Bích/Dong Son bronze drums, Chinese domination 111 BCE-939 CE, Trưng Sisters rebellion, Ly/Tran/Le dynasties, Mongol invasions repelled, Champa conflicts, Tây Sơn rebellion, Nguyễn Dynasty, French colonization (Indochina 1887-1954), WWII Japanese occupation, Hồ Chí Minh's independence 1945, First Indochina War 1946-54 (Diện Biên Phủ), partition, Vietnam War 1955-1975 (3M+ dead), Fall of Saigon 1975, reunification, Đổi Mới reforms 1986, and recent economic growth under CPV.

religion.note: Ancestor worship/folk religion dominant; Mahayana Buddhism; Confucian/Taoist syncretism; Catholic legacy (8%; Diệm and Ngô family Catholic); Cao Dai (syncretic, Tay Ninh); Hoa Hao (Buddhist reform, Mekong); CPV officially atheist but tolerates religion

ethnic_groups.name: Kinh (Viet)
ethnic_groups.notes: Ethnic Vietnamese; Austroasiatic; Red River/Mekong deltas; politically dominant; Han Chinese cultural influence (Confucian, sinographic script historically); Vietnam War 'Vietnamese'; CPV

ethnic_groups.name: Tay
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern highlands; Tai-Kadai; second-largest minority; rice terraces; cross-border with China

ethnic_groups.name: Thai
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwest; Tai-Kadai; Black Thai, White Thai subgroups; distinct from Thailand Thais

ethnic_groups.name: Muong
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern mountains; Austroasiatic; linguistically close to Kinh; Hoa Binh area

ethnic_groups.name: Khmer Krom
ethnic_groups.notes: Mekong Delta; ethnic Khmer; Theravada Buddhist; ~1.3M; annexed from Cambodia (Cochinchina); Cambodian grievance; some discrimination

ethnic_groups.name: Hmong (Mong)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern highlands; Hmong-Mien; fought with French/US (some); Sapa; opium historically; cross-border

ethnic_groups.name: Hoa (Chinese)
ethnic_groups.notes: Ethnic Chinese; Cantonese/Teochew; Saigon/Cholon (Chinatown); merchants; many fled 1978-79 (boat people, anti-Chinese campaign); now ~1M

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Dao, Gia Rai, Ede, Ba Na, Cham, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: 53 officially recognized ethnic groups; Dao (Yao); Gia Rai/Ede (Central Highlands, Austronesian, Montagnard, US allies Vietnam War); Cham (Muslim/Hindu, remnant of Champa kingdom); diverse hill tribes

independence.date: 1945-09-02 (declared from Japan), 1954-07-21 (recognized after First Indochina War), 1975-04-30 (reunification)
independence.from: France (1954), reunified after defeating South Vietnam/US (1975)

country_profile.notes_unique: Vietnam War (American War, 1955-75, ~3M dead including 58,000 US); Fall of Saigon April 30, 1975 (iconic helicopter); Hồ Chí Minh (Uncle Ho, independence icon); Diện Biên Phủ 1954 (French defeated); boat people (1978-80s refugees); Agent Orange (dioxin, birth defects); Cu Chi tunnels; My Lai massacre; Đổi Mới 1986 (economic reforms, market socialism); one-party CPV rule; Hanoi vs Saigon (HCMC) divide; pho, bánh mì; South China Sea disputes (Spratly/Paracel)

current_leader.name: Tô Lâm
current_leader.title: General Secretary of CPV & President
current_leader.notes: Public Security background; anti-corruption czar; consolidated power; holds both top posts (unusual); conservative; CPV collective leadership model

prime_minister.name: Phạm Minh Chính
prime_minister.title: Prime Minister
prime_minister.notes: Public Security background; COVID-19 response; economic management; Hanoi faction

former_leaders.name: Nguyễn Phú Trọng
former_leaders.notes: General Secretary; longest-serving leader since Hồ; anti-corruption 'blazing furnace'; conservative; died July 2024; also President 2018-2021; Hanoi faction

former_leaders.name: Nguyễn Tấn Dũng
former_leaders.notes: PM (nominal #2, PM has executive role); southern; economic reforms; lost power struggle to Trọng

former_leaders.name: Nông Đức Mạnh
former_leaders.notes: General Secretary; ethnic Tay; consensus builder; WTO accession 2007

former_leaders.name: Lê Khả Phiêu
former_leaders.notes: General Secretary; hardliner; conservative; Asian financial crisis

former_leaders.name: Võ Văn Kiệt
former_leaders.notes: PM; ethnic Chinese-Vietnamese; economic architect; Đổi Mới implementation

former_leaders.name: Nguyễn Văn Linh
former_leaders.notes: General Secretary; launched Đổi Mới (Renovation, market reforms); southern; pragmatist

former_leaders.name: Trường Chinh
former_leaders.notes: Ideologue; land reform disaster 1950s (~10,000 killed); briefly General Secretary

former_leaders.name: Lê Duẩn
former_leaders.notes: General Secretary; Vietnam War leader; hardliner; southern guerrilla commander; reunification architect; died 1986

former_leaders.name: Hồ Chí Minh (Uncle Ho)
former_leaders.notes: Founding father; President; independence hero; Diện Biên Phủ; Vietnam War; died September 1969 (before Fall of Saigon); mausoleum in Hanoi; cult of personality; Saigon renamed HCMC; revered

former_leaders.name: Võ Nguyên Giáp
former_leaders.notes: General (not head of state); Diện Biên Phủ victor; military genius; Defense Minister; 'Red Napoleon'; Tết Offensive; died 2013; national hero

910.name: Prehistoric Vietnam and Dong Son
910.description: Early human habitation in Vietnam, the Hoabinhian culture, the Phung Nguyen civilization, and the remarkable Dong Son Bronze Age culture famous for its bronze drums.

sub_clusters.name: Early Settlement and Hoabinhian Culture
sub_clusters.description: Homo erectus remains in northern Vietnam, the Hoabinhian technocomplex of cave-dwelling hunter-gatherers, and the transition to agricultural communities in the Red River delta.

sub_clusters.name: Dong Son Bronze Culture
sub_clusters.description: The Dong Son civilization's extraordinary bronze drums, its sophisticated wet-rice agriculture, the legendary Hong Bang dynasty and Van Lang kingdom, and the Au Lac state under An Duong Vuong.
key_events: Dong Son bronze drums — masterpieces of Southeast Asian metallurgy — created (c. 600 BC onward)
An Duong Vuong founds the Au Lac state and builds the Co Loa citadel (c. 257 BC)

910.name: Chinese Domination Period
910.description: Over a thousand years of Chinese rule — the Nanyue kingdom, the Han conquest, the Trung Sisters' rebellion, the development of Vietnamese identity under Chinese administration, and the final independence.

sub_clusters.name: Nanyue and Han Conquest
sub_clusters.description: Zhao Tuo's Nanyue kingdom incorporating Vietnam, the Han dynasty's conquest and imposition of direct rule, Chinese cultural and administrative assimilation, and the simmering Vietnamese resistance.
key_events: Zhao Tuo establishes the Nanyue kingdom encompassing northern Vietnam (207 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Trung Sisters and Vietnamese Resistance
sub_clusters.description: The Trung Sisters' rebellion — Vietnam's most celebrated act of resistance, Lady Trieu's revolt, the Ly Bi rebellion and the early Ly dynasty, and the continuous struggle for independence.
key_events: Trung Sisters lead a major rebellion against Han rule and briefly establish an independent state (40–43 AD)
Lady Trieu (Bà Triệu) leads another revolt against Chinese Wu rule (248 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Tang Rule and Independence
sub_clusters.description: Vietnam under Tang dynasty rule as the Protectorate of Annan, the development of a distinctive Vietnamese culture despite Sinification, and Ngo Quyen's decisive Battle of Bach Dang River.
key_events: Ngo Quyen defeats the Southern Han fleet at the Battle of Bach Dang River, ending Chinese rule (938 AD)

920.name: Independent Dynasties and Dai Viet
920.description: The establishment of independent Vietnamese dynasties — Ngo, Dinh, Early Le, Ly, and Tran — the creation of Dai Viet as a major power, the repulsion of Mongol invasions, and Vietnamese high culture.

sub_clusters.name: Early Independent Dynasties
sub_clusters.description: The Ngo, Dinh, and Early Le dynasties establishing Vietnamese independence, the twelve warlords period, and the consolidation of centralized rule in the Red River delta.

sub_clusters.name: Ly Dynasty Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: The Ly dynasty's founding of Thang Long (Hanoi), the construction of the Temple of Literature, the development of Vietnamese Buddhism, the defeat of Song Chinese invasions, and the Nam tien southward expansion.
key_events: Ly Thai To moves the capital to Thang Long (modern Hanoi) (1010)
Temple of Literature founded — one of Vietnam's first universities (1070)

sub_clusters.name: Tran Dynasty and Mongol Invasions
sub_clusters.description: The Tran dynasty's remarkable repulsion of three Mongol invasions by Kublai Khan, Tran Hung Dao's brilliant military leadership, and the development of chu nom Vietnamese script.
key_events: Tran Hung Dao defeats three Mongol invasions (1258, 1285, 1288)
Battle of Bach Dang (1288) — Tran Hung Dao uses iron-tipped stakes to destroy the Mongol fleet

930.name: Ming Occupation and Le Dynasty
930.description: The brief Ming Chinese occupation, Le Loi's liberation war, the great Le dynasty, the legal code of Le Thanh Tong, and the apogee of Confucian Vietnamese civilization.

sub_clusters.name: Ming Occupation and Le Loi's Liberation
sub_clusters.description: The Ho dynasty's overthrow of the Tran, the Ming Chinese invasion and occupation, Le Loi's ten-year guerrilla war of liberation aided by Nguyen Trai, and the founding of the Le dynasty.
key_events: Le Loi defeats the Ming Chinese and founds the Le dynasty (1428)
Nguyen Trai's Great Proclamation upon Victory — a masterpiece of Vietnamese literature

sub_clusters.name: Le Thanh Tong's Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: The reign of Le Thanh Tong, the Hong Duc legal code, administrative reforms modeled on the Ming, the conquest of Champa, and the continued Nam tien southward expansion.
key_events: Le Thanh Tong promulgates the Hong Duc legal code (1483)
Vietnamese conquer the Cham capital Vijaya, effectively ending the Champa kingdom (1471)

930.name: Trinh-Nguyen Division
930.description: Vietnam's long period of division between the Trinh lords in the north and the Nguyen lords in the south, European missionary activity, the Tay Son rebellion, and the eventual reunification.

sub_clusters.name: Trinh-Nguyen Lords
sub_clusters.description: The Mac dynasty usurpation, the Le restoration, the division between the Trinh in Tonkin and the Nguyen in Cochinchina, the Nguyen southward expansion into Khmer territory, and the arrival of Jesuit missionaries.
key_events: Alexandre de Rhodes develops the Romanized Vietnamese script (quoc ngu) (1651)

sub_clusters.name: Tay Son Rebellion and Reunification
sub_clusters.description: The Tay Son brothers' peasant rebellion overthrowing both the Trinh and Nguyen lords, Emperor Quang Trung's brilliant defeat of a Chinese Qing invasion, and Nguyen Anh's eventual victory with French aid.
key_events: Quang Trung defeats a 200,000-strong Qing Chinese invasion at the Battle of Ngoc Hoi-Dong Da (1789)
Nguyen Anh defeats the Tay Son and establishes the Nguyen dynasty as Emperor Gia Long (1802)

940.name: Nguyen Dynasty and French Conquest
940.description: The Nguyen dynasty's unification and Confucian conservatism, the construction of the Hue Imperial City, Minh Mang's persecution of Christians, and the French military conquest of Indochina.

sub_clusters.name: Nguyen Dynasty and Imperial Hue
sub_clusters.description: Gia Long's unification and naming of 'Viet Nam', the construction of the Imperial City at Hue modeled on Beijing's Forbidden City, Minh Mang's centralization and persecution of Christians.
key_events: Emperor Gia Long unifies Vietnam and establishes the imperial capital at Hue (1802)

sub_clusters.name: French Conquest of Indochina
sub_clusters.description: The French attack on Da Nang and seizure of Saigon, the progressive conquest of Cochinchina, Annam, and Tonkin, the Can Vuong resistance movement, and the creation of French Indochina.
key_events: French forces capture Saigon (1859)
Treaty of Hue makes Annam and Tonkin French protectorates (1884)

940.name: French Indochina
940.description: Vietnam under French colonial rule, the exploitation of rice, rubber, and minerals, the rise of Vietnamese nationalism, Ho Chi Minh, and the founding of the Viet Minh.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Exploitation and Nationalist Awakening
sub_clusters.description: The French colonial economic exploitation, the corvée labor system, Phan Boi Chau and Phan Chu Trinh's reform movements, Ho Chi Minh's journey abroad, and the founding of the Indochinese Communist Party.
key_events: Ho Chi Minh founds the Indochinese Communist Party (1930)
Yen Bai mutiny — VNQDD-led uprising brutally suppressed (1930)

sub_clusters.name: World War II and Viet Minh
sub_clusters.description: Japanese occupation alongside Vichy French administration, the catastrophic 1944–1945 famine killing up to 2 million, Ho Chi Minh's founding of the Viet Minh, and the August Revolution.
key_events: Vietnamese famine kills an estimated 1–2 million people (1944–1945)
Ho Chi Minh declares Vietnamese independence, quoting the US Declaration of Independence (2 September 1945)

950.name: First Indochina War
950.description: The Viet Minh's war against France, General Giap's brilliant guerrilla and conventional campaigns, the devastating French defeat at Dien Bien Phu, and the Geneva Accords partitioning Vietnam.

sub_clusters.name: French Return and War
sub_clusters.description: The failed negotiations between Ho Chi Minh and France, the French bombardment of Haiphong, the outbreak of full-scale war, the Viet Minh's guerrilla strategy, and Mao's Chinese Communist victory providing aid.

sub_clusters.name: Dien Bien Phu and Geneva Accords
sub_clusters.description: American aid to France, Giap's siege of Dien Bien Phu, the catastrophic French defeat, and the Geneva Accords dividing Vietnam at the 17th parallel.
key_events: Battle of Dien Bien Phu — Viet Minh defeat the French in one of history's most decisive battles (March–May 1954)
Geneva Accords partition Vietnam at the 17th parallel (July 1954)

950.name: Vietnam War (Second Indochina War)
950.description: The American War — Diem's Republic of Vietnam, the NLF insurgency, massive US military intervention, the Tet Offensive, the anti-war movement, Vietnamization, and the fall of Saigon.

sub_clusters.name: Diem Era and US Escalation
sub_clusters.description: Ngo Dinh Diem's authoritarian rule, the Buddhist crisis, the self-immolation of Thich Quang Duc, Diem's assassination, the Gulf of Tonkin incident, and the deployment of US combat troops.
key_events: Buddhist monk Thich Quang Duc's self-immolation shocks the world (June 1963)
Gulf of Tonkin incident leads to direct US military involvement (August 1964)

sub_clusters.name: Tet Offensive and Peak US Involvement
sub_clusters.description: The deployment of over 500,000 US troops, Operation Rolling Thunder bombing, the search-and-destroy strategy, the My Lai massacre, and the Tet Offensive that turned American public opinion.
key_events: Tet Offensive — NLF and NVA launch coordinated attacks across South Vietnam (January 1968)
My Lai massacre — US soldiers kill hundreds of Vietnamese civilians (March 1968)

sub_clusters.name: Vietnamization and Fall of Saigon
sub_clusters.description: Nixon's Vietnamization policy, the Paris Peace Accords, the withdrawal of US forces, the Easter Offensive, and the North Vietnamese final offensive culminating in the fall of Saigon.
key_events: Paris Peace Accords signed; US withdraws combat forces (January 1973)
Fall of Saigon — North Vietnamese tanks enter the Presidential Palace; Vietnam reunified (30 April 1975)

960.name: Reunification and Isolation
960.description: The reunification of Vietnam, socialist transformation of the south, the refugee boat people crisis, the invasion of Cambodia, the Sino-Vietnamese War, and economic hardship.

sub_clusters.name: Socialist Transformation
sub_clusters.description: The reunification as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, re-education camps, collectivization of southern agriculture, the exodus of boat people, and the Third Indochina War.
key_events: Vietnam invades Cambodia and topples the Khmer Rouge (December 1978–January 1979)
Sino-Vietnamese War — China invades Vietnam's northern border (February–March 1979)

sub_clusters.name: International Isolation and Economic Crisis
sub_clusters.description: International sanctions over Cambodia, the US trade embargo, economic stagnation, the boat people exodus continuing, and the growing recognition that reform was essential.

960.name: Doi Moi and Modern Vietnam
960.description: The Doi Moi economic renovation, Vietnam's dramatic transformation from one of the world's poorest countries to a middle-income tiger economy, WTO membership, and geopolitical rebalancing.

sub_clusters.name: Doi Moi Reforms and Opening
sub_clusters.description: The 1986 Doi Moi economic renovation, the shift to a 'socialist-oriented market economy', the withdrawal from Cambodia, normalization with China and the US, ASEAN membership, and rapid poverty reduction.
key_events: Doi Moi economic reforms launched at the Sixth Party Congress (December 1986)
US normalizes diplomatic relations with Vietnam (July 1995)

sub_clusters.name: Economic Tiger and Global Integration
sub_clusters.description: Vietnam's WTO accession, the manufacturing and FDI boom, the South China Sea tensions, the Comprehensive Partnership with the US, the Trans-Pacific trade agreements, and Vietnam's emergence as a major economy.
key_events: Vietnam joins the WTO (January 2007)
Vietnam and the US upgrade to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (September 2023)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
